data.title: Sibanye-Stillwater Earnings Call: Record Profits, Real Risks
data.description:
Sibanye- Stillwater Limited ((SBYSF)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Sibanye-Stillwater’s latest earnings call struck an emphatically upbeat tone despite clear operational and macro risks. Management highlighted record revenue, EBITDA, cash generation and earnings, alongside rapid debt reduction and a dividend at the top end of policy. These gains contrasted with sobering comments on fatalities, higher costs, and lingering uncertainty around U.S. incentives and global growth.

Record Group Revenue and EBITDA Expansion

Six-month group revenue came in just under ZAR 90 billion, a 64% jump year-on-year, reflecting broad-based strength across commodities and regions. Adjusted EBITDA surged 111% to ZAR 31.8 billion, delivering a 35% margin, while profit climbed 581%, underscoring powerful operational leverage in the current price environment.

Promotion

55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Robust Cash Generation and Balance Sheet Strength

Operational cash generation increased 531% to nearly ZAR 21 billion, translating into a healthy 65% EBITDA-to-cash conversion rate and record net operating cash for the period. Gross debt fell 18% in six months to ZAR 32.1 billion, with net gearing at 0.18x and roughly ZAR 48 billion of liquidity headroom, leaving the maturity profile described as very manageable.

Commodity Price Tailwinds Across Key Markets

Results were strongly supported by higher commodity prices, with both South African and U.S. PGM baskets up about 70% year-on-year and local gold prices up 35%. Australian zinc also contributed, with a 25% price increase lifting profitability at the Century operation despite its near-end-of-life status.

South African PGM: Solid Delivery and Strong Margins

South African PGM production of 790,000 4E ounces matched guidance even as volumes were 2% lower year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA from these assets rose to ZAR 19.2 billion, up 302%, and delivered a 44% all-in sustaining cost margin and 45% EBITDA margin, supported by higher basket prices and chrome byproduct credits.

PGM Cash Flow and Chrome’s Growing Role

Notional free cash flow from South African PGMs reached ZAR 10.4 billion, a ZAR 9.9 billion improvement year-on-year and a 54% conversion from EBITDA. Chrome contributed ZAR 1.1 billion in operating profit, and management expects a larger impact as UG2 feed is prioritized, even though chrome production dipped 18% after the planned closure of the BTT concentrator.

Record Earnings from South African Gold

South African gold sold rose 5% while the average gold price climbed 35%, driving adjusted EBITDA to a record ZAR 9 billion, up 87% year-on-year and yielding a 39% margin. Notional free cash flow of ZAR 3.9 billion reflected a 267% increase in cash generation, highlighting the earnings power of the gold segment in the current price cycle.

Surface Gold and DRDGOLD’s Performance

Surface gold output grew 13% to 105,000 ounces and now accounts for 36% of the South African gold mix, diversifying the production base. DRDGOLD produced 2.5 tonnes of gold with a 10% yield improvement, while Cooke’s production increased 11% on third-party material, bolstering overall surface contributions.

Burnstone Project: Long-Life, High-Return Gold

The Board approved the Burnstone project, envisioned to deliver roughly 130,000 ounces of gold per year at steady state over a 25-year life. With total project capital of around ZAR 6.2 billion, it carries a net present value of ZAR 19.2 billion and an internal rate of return of 36%, supported by existing shaft and surface infrastructure and a modest ZAR 98 million capital allocation in 2026.

Mount Lyell: Copper-Gold Growth in Tasmania

Mount Lyell, a copper-gold project in Tasmania, also received Board approval with total capital to production of about USD 340 million and a net present value of roughly USD 550 million. The 23-year project is expected to support around 300 steady-state jobs and deliver long-term copper and gold output, further diversifying Sibanye-Stillwater’s commodity and geographic exposure.

Dividend at Upper End of Payout Policy

The Board declared an interim dividend of ZAR 5.7 billion, or ZAR 2.01 per share, placing the payout at the upper end of the 25% to 35% normalized earnings policy range. The annualized dividend yield sits near 8% with a trailing 12-month yield of 6.6%, though management noted the policy is slightly below peers and is unlikely to rise materially until gross debt is cut by half.

U.S. PGM: Mechanization Progress Amid EBITDA Pressure

U.S. PGM production of 138,000 ounces of palladium and platinum was in line with guidance, and mechanized bolting trials at Stillwater East, along with operating-model work, advanced as planned. However, adjusted EBITDA dropped 56% to USD 66 million, with all-in sustaining costs up 12% to USD 1,347 per ounce, partly due to investment in mechanization and a tough comparison versus last year’s large Section 45X tax credit.

Improved U.S. Cash Performance Despite Investment

Notional free cash flow from U.S. PGMs remained negative at USD 28 million but represented a 52% reduction in cash outflow year-to-date. Higher palladium and platinum prices helped, while cash was deliberately deployed to fund mechanization, which management sees as critical to achieving a sustainable cost base.

Recycling Business: Scale and Margin Expansion

The recycling segment posted a 13% adjusted EBITDA margin, generating USD 164 million in adjusted EBITDA and USD 103 million in cash, a 63% conversion rate. Precious metals production jumped 142% year-on-year to about 2.8 million gold-equivalent ounces, underscoring the growing scale and strategic importance of this lower-capex, high-cash-flow business.

Century Zinc: Strong Cash, Limited Life

Century produced 45 kilotonnes of payable zinc, in line with guidance, and delivered USD 55 million of adjusted EBITDA, up 54% year-on-year, with notional free cash flow of USD 41 million, up 86%. Yet management stressed Century is nearing end of life, with an estimated 12 to 18 months of mining left and costs 23% higher year-on-year at USD 2,162 per tonne.

Keliber Lithium: Mining Progress, Refinery Decision Pending

At Keliber, mining is fully underway with 218 kilotonnes extracted and 186 kilotonnes added to the strategic stockpile, exceeding milestones and meeting targeted run rates. Concentrator commissioning is in progress and capital spending of EUR 719 million remains on plan against a EUR 783 million budget, but the decision to start the refinery still depends on concentrator performance and lithium market conditions.

Organic Growth Pipeline and Capital Discipline

The approved organic growth pipeline includes Thembelani, Siphumelele, Western Limb Tailings Retreatment, Burnstone and Mount Lyell, which collectively underpin production over the next five years. Management emphasized disciplined sequencing based on returns, affordability, readiness and strategic fit, even as operating-model changes across a multi-acquisition portfolio take longer than initially expected.

Renewable Energy and Water Independence Initiatives

Sibanye-Stillwater already has more than 165 megawatts of renewable energy in operation and expects this to exceed 835 megawatts by 2028, potentially saving over ZAR 1 billion in energy costs and bringing about half of power needs under its control. Water independence is improving, with South African gold operations at 95% and PGM operations at 42%, and plans to lift PGM water independence to 90% by 2028.

Safety Metrics Improve but Fatalities Persist

Safety indicators continue to trend downward, and management said performance compares favorably to both the company’s history and peers, noting Driefontein’s year without a fatal incident. However, three colleagues were lost to safety incidents and three to crime-related events in the quarter, which the company described as preventable challenges that remain a central focus.

Operational Headwinds in Gold and PGM Segments

South African PGM production was 2% lower year-on-year and all-in sustaining costs rose 10% to ZAR 26,252 per 4E ounce, driven by royalties, inflation and consumables despite chrome credits. South African gold output slipped 2% to 294,000 ounces, with underground volumes down 9% and costs higher due to shaft maintenance, winder upgrades, reserve development, water pumping, plant upgrades and double handling.

Kloof and Beatrix: Seismic and Infrastructure Challenges

Kloof 7 was closed and the broader Kloof operation rebased to reduce exposure to highly seismic ground, limiting access to some higher-grade areas but improving risk management. At Beatrix, seismic damage to footwall infrastructure cut off high-grade zones, although plant recoveries are now improving after maintenance intervention, suggesting gradual operational normalization.

Labor Negotiations and Mechanization Execution Risk

Two union labor agreements covering Stillwater and East Boulder remain under negotiation, complicated by the mechanization program’s impact on work practices, equipment use and team-based incentives. Management warned the mechanization process is multi-year and depends on workforce adoption and supervisory capability, adding that capital will not be heavily committed to future areas if targeted cost levels cannot be achieved.

Macroeconomic and Lithium Market Uncertainty

Management flagged macro and geopolitical risks, including conflict in the Middle East, weaker global growth forecasts and trade disruptions that could weigh on investment and industrial demand. Battery-grade lithium hydroxide prices fell 9% in the quarter and are expected to ease further as new supply arrives, although management does not foresee prices dropping below 2025 levels.

Section 45X Timing and Portfolio Simplification Delays

The U.S. tax authority has begun reviewing the 2023 return linked to the Section 45X credit and requested additional information and a potential site visit, leaving cash timing uncertain. Separately, management acknowledged that reshaping a portfolio built through multiple acquisitions is taking longer than anticipated, and that several simplification initiatives have not yet reached announcement stage.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Strategic Priorities

Management said the company remains on track to meet operational and financial guidance, with South African PGM output at 790,000 4E ounces and second-half costs set to rise but stay within the guided range. Century’s costs sit at the lower end of guidance, gold unit cost guidance has been lifted, lithium prices are expected to soften modestly, Stillwater is targeting USD 1,000 per ounce by 2028, and Burnstone and Mount Lyell are being developed under defined capital and life-of-mine frameworks, all while management works to reduce gross debt by 50% over two to three years within a firm dividend policy.

Sibanye-Stillwater’s call painted a picture of a miner enjoying a powerful earnings and cash upswing, yet acutely aware of safety, cost and macro risks. For investors, the combination of strong current returns, disciplined capital deployment and clear balance-sheet priorities, tempered by execution and market uncertainties, frames a compelling but not risk-free long-term story.

data.title: Medacta Earnings Call: Strong Growth, Tight Margins
data.description:
Medacta Group Sa ((CH:MOVE)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Medacta’s latest earnings call painted a broadly upbeat picture despite notable headwinds. Management highlighted nearly 10% constant-currency revenue growth, above-market performance across most product lines and regions, and reaffirmed 2026 and midterm targets. Yet, margin compression, weaker cash generation, and U.S.-specific challenges tempered the tone, with executives conceding that hitting the midpoint of full-year guidance will be demanding.

Strong Top Line and EBITDA, But Margins Under Pressure

Medacta delivered a robust first half, with constant-currency revenue up almost 10% to EUR 368 million and adjusted EBITDA at EUR 97 million. The margin reached 27.8% in constant currency and 26.5% on a reported basis, underscoring solid profitability, though investors will note the squeeze versus prior periods as cost and mix effects weighed on the P&L.

Promotion

55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Comparable Net Profit Holds Up Despite FX and One-Offs

Reported net profit fell to EUR 42 million, or 11.4% of revenue, down from EUR 60 million a year earlier. Management stressed that last year benefited from a one-off purchase gain and that this year absorbed about EUR 7 million in negative FX, leaving comparable net profit at EUR 49 million versus EUR 46 million, signaling underlying earnings resilience.

Geographic Expansion Drives Broad-Based Growth

Growth was well diversified across regions, with EMEA up 10%, APAC rising 13.1%, and Latin America jumping 16.4%, all well above typical industry rates. North America trailed with roughly 7% growth, reflecting a slower U.S. market backdrop, but still outpaced the estimated 3% market growth, showing share gains despite local challenges.

Portfolio Performance Remains Above Market Across Segments

All key product categories posted gains in the first half, with hips up around 8%, knees almost 11%, extremities nearly 16%, and spine 4.5%. Management emphasized that hip, knee, extremities, and spine businesses are growing faster than their respective markets, reinforcing Medacta’s positioning as a share taker in core orthopedics.

Hip Innovation Accelerates Growth With New Launches

Hip products continued to outperform, with growth described at roughly twice the market, supported by Medacta’s innovation pipeline. NextAR Hip entered limited release in the U.S. and Australia, while the Infinity triple-tapered stem moved to full rollout and gained traction in the U.S. and Japan, providing fresh catalysts for future volumes.

Knee Business Powered by Kinematic Alignment Strategy

The knee segment grew almost 11%, driven by Medacta’s focus on Kinematic Alignment and the GMK SpheriKA implant. Management said GMK SpheriKA is rapidly becoming its most important knee product, with segment growth running more than twice the market, underlining strong surgeon adoption of the alignment concept.

Extremities Surge With New Shoulder and Sports Medicine Tools

Extremities delivered standout performance, rising almost 16% and more than double market growth. The company rolled out revision shoulder arthroplasty in the U.S., began international expansion, and introduced the AI-based MyShoulder Planner, alongside Secure-Fix, an all-inside meniscal repair system that is expected to be a key driver in knee sports medicine.

Spine Technology Adoption and Shift to a More Profitable Model

In spine, enabling technology now accounts for roughly 50% of U.S. revenues, reflecting growing adoption of technology-supported procedures. Medacta is pivoting to a more direct and more exclusive agent model in the U.S., while spine profitability has moved from breakeven to positive, though still around a third of the margin of the core joint business.

India Approval Opens a New High-Growth Market

Medacta secured approval for its knee products in India just before the call and plans to begin shipping in September. Management sees India as a market with around EUR 100 million current potential and growth above 15%, albeit at low European pricing levels, adding a sizable emerging-market growth leg to the story.

U.S. Recovery Efforts and New Product Momentum

In the U.S., the company reported re-acceleration in hips tied to the triple-tapered stem, continued solid knee growth, and good traction from the new Monoblock shoulder stem. Medacta expects reduced spine dilution and believes base-customer attrition should ease thanks to a growing pipeline of new surgeons and accounts.

Ongoing Investment in Capacity and U.S. Infrastructure

CapEx reached EUR 74 million in H1, including EUR 42 million for instruments, EUR 22 million for tangible assets, EUR 8 million for R&D, and EUR 2 million for other items. Tangible investments focus on expanding production capacity, land, and buildings, aligning with plans for future manufacturing scale and staffing growth.

New U.S. Headquarters and Manufacturing Expansion in Tennessee

To support its accelerating U.S. development, Medacta acquired a large site in Tennessee for new headquarters and domestic manufacturing. This move should shorten supply chains and deepen local presence in the company’s most strategically important market, potentially boosting competitiveness and responsiveness to customers over time.

In-House Innovation Favored Over Large M&A

Management reiterated its preference for internal development, saying it delivers better returns on capital than big-ticket acquisitions. Medacta is building its own spine technology and robotics platform at a fraction of the cost of a peer’s large spine deal, while remaining open to smaller sports medicine and niche opportunities that fit its strategy.

Cost Discipline Helps Offset Gross Margin Erosion

Although costs had initially been set for higher anticipated growth, the company has since aligned spending with actual revenue trends. Management emphasized its ability to adjust operating expenses, noting that careful cost control partially offset the impact of gross margin erosion and helped preserve profitability.

Gross Margin Hit by FX, Pricing, and Mix Effects

Gross profit rose to EUR 240 million from EUR 233 million, but the margin dropped to 65.2% from 68.3%, a roughly 3-point decline. The fall was attributed to a 1.3% adverse FX impact, about 0.5% price erosion, and around 1.3% from geographic and product mix, including lower U.S. sales, higher sports medicine volumes, and a higher D&A ratio.

EBITDA Margin Pressure Reflects Limited Leverage

At constant currency, adjusted EBITDA margin slipped 0.9 percentage points from the prior semester once FX effects are stripped out. Management cited gross profit erosion as the main driver, with only modest operating leverage from higher volumes and cost discipline, signaling that margin expansion remains a work in progress.

Reported Earnings and Cash Flow Weaken, Leverage Ticks Up

Operating cash flow fell to about EUR 56 million from EUR 73 million, as EBITDA softness and higher working capital needs weighed on cash generation. Investing outflows of EUR 74 million produced negative free cash flow of EUR 18.6 million, and net debt leverage rose to 1.2x adjusted EBITDA from 0.9x at year-end, though still at conservative levels.

U.S. Market Slows, Customer Attrition and Spanish Strikes Bite

Management estimated U.S. market growth at only around 3% versus expected 5%–5.5%, dampening North American momentum. Base attrition among existing U.S. customers and surgeon shifts toward ambulatory centers hurt volumes, while public-sector strikes in Spain left that market down nearly 20%, even as Medacta’s Spanish unit still grew.

Spine and Sports Medicine Still Dilutive to Group Margins

Spine grew 4.5%, a subdued pace as Medacta transitions to a more profitable model focused on specialty products and technology-enabled sales. Sports medicine remains loss-making as the company invests in sales-force expansion and product development, and management flagged both spine and sports medicine as segments that must scale to reduce EBITDA dilution.

External Transportation Costs Add to Margin Headwinds

Fuel surcharges on external transportation have pushed up variable logistics costs, providing another drag on margins that management says is largely outside its control. Elevated fuel prices exacerbate cost pressure at a time when FX, pricing, and mix are already weighing on profitability, limiting near-term relief for gross margins.

Instrument Deployment Drives Higher D&A in a Softer Top Line

The D&A ratio increased because the company had placed a similar level of instruments into the market despite lower-than-expected revenues. These instruments were originally deployed for a stronger growth scenario, and management signaled that it may pull back some incremental instruments in the second half to ease the burden.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Market Context

Medacta reaffirmed its 2026 outlook for 10%–14% revenue growth and around 50 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin expansion in constant currency, as well as midterm revenue CAGR of 12%–15% with gradual EBITDA improvement. Management said hitting the midpoint remains possible but more likely slightly below, noting that even 10%–12% growth would be nearly three times current market rates.

Medacta’s earnings call ultimately balanced strong growth and strategic progress against margin and cash-flow challenges. The company continues to outpace the market, backed by innovation, geographic diversification, and capacity expansion, while openly acknowledging pressure points in the U.S., spine, and sports medicine. For investors, the story remains one of above-market growth with a clear focus on improving profitability.

data.title: New Hope Corporation Earnings Call Highlights Strong Cash
data.description:
New Hope Corporation Limited ((AU:NHC)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

New Hope Corporation’s latest earnings call struck a confident tone, underpinned by record cash generation, stronger EBITDA and production beating guidance. Management highlighted robust performances at Bengalla and New Acland, but balanced the optimism with candid discussion of rising high‑potential safety events, rail disruptions, quarterly cost volatility and persistent inflationary pressure.

Fourth-Quarter EBITDA Surge

Underlying EBITDA jumped to $169 million in the fourth quarter, a 30% rise from the prior quarter. Management credited better realized pricing, with supportive benchmark index moves and favourable foreign‑exchange effects, underscoring the leverage of New Hope’s operations to thermal coal markets.

Promotion

55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Full-Year Production Beats Guidance

For FY2026, saleable coal production reached 11.5 million tonnes, up 8% on FY2025 and above the group’s guidance range. The result signals a successful ramp‑up across key assets and provides a stronger production base to support earnings and cash generation in a volatile energy market.

Strong Cash Generation and EBITDA

Operational cash flows for FY2026 totaled $564 million, alongside underlying EBITDA of $514 million. Management linked the cash strength to elevated coal prices and higher volumes, reinforcing the balance sheet and supporting both investment in growth projects and ongoing capital management.

Bengalla’s Strong Operational Finish

Bengalla recorded raw coal output of 3.0 million tonnes in the quarter, up 16% on the previous period, with saleable coal at 2.3 million tonnes, up 8%. The mine hit targeted raw production of 13.4 million tonnes on a 100% basis, capping off a strong quarter that helped drive group performance.

Bengalla Volumes Exceed Full-Year Guidance

Over FY2026, Bengalla delivered 8.2 million tonnes of saleable coal and coal sales, surpassing its guidance range. The outperformance followed a recovery from severe Hunter region weather late in FY2025, highlighting the mine’s resilience and operational flexibility after disruption.

Bengalla Costs at Guidance Floor

Bengalla’s FY2026 FOB cash cost came in at $81.30 per sales tonne, at the lower end of the $81 to $89 guidance range. Achieving cost performance at the guidance floor in an inflationary environment underscores solid cost discipline and supports margins even as prices and demand fluctuate.

New Acland Ramp-Up Continues

New Acland produced 1.7 million tonnes of raw coal in the quarter, up 3% on the prior period. FY2026 saleable production was 3.3 million tonnes, a 17% increase year on year, demonstrating steady progress in ramping the operation toward its longer‑term capacity targets.

New Acland Sales Above Guidance

Coal sales from New Acland reached 3.6 million tonnes in FY2026, exceeding guidance. Management said increased spot rail capacity during the year supported the stronger sales outcome, although they noted that logistics constraints remain an operating risk.

Advancing New Acland Growth Plans

The operation is ramping toward a 5 million tonnes per annum target, with access to the Manning Vale West pit scheduled for the second half of calendar 2026. First coal is expected shortly after, positioning New Acland as a growing contributor to group volumes over the medium term.

Low Strip Ratios Underpin Mine Economics

Bengalla’s strip ratio was about 4 in the quarter, and management expects it to stay in the 4s on average for the mine life. New Acland is also expected to average around a 4 strip ratio, supporting efficient waste movement and favourable long‑run operating economics.

Flexible Wash Strategy Protects Margins

Management highlighted an upgraded wash‑plant that allows switching between high‑ash and low‑ash coal, depending on market discounts. This flexible wash strategy aims to maximize profitability by tailoring product quality to prevailing demand and pricing conditions.

Optimizing Capital Expenditure

The group has deferred some sustaining capital via overhaul management, asset productivity initiatives and careful maintenance planning. Management stressed a focus on minimizing capex where possible while balancing the risk of unplanned breakdowns against equipment reliability needs.

Lower Capital Needs After Key Projects

Around $130 million has been earmarked to complete the Manning Vale West pit, including road realignment and fleet spending. Once this and additional Bengalla investment are finished, management expects capital requirements to moderate even as production continues to grow.

Shareholder Returns Backed by Cash and Franking

Management noted that cash balances are materially above the desired long‑term level and highlighted a significant franking account balance. They indicated that shareholders should continue to see rewards, pointing to the expectation of a reasonable dividend supported by strong cash flows.

Malabar Ramp-Up and Portfolio Optionality

At Malabar, the Maxwell Mine’s longwall is operating and productivity is expected to keep ramping up. Management said the operation should become cash generative in the near future, while newly acquired Mount Arthur tenements add optionality for longer‑term portfolio development.

Emerging Malabar Infrastructure Opportunities

Management flagged potential data‑center and battery‑related infrastructure opportunities tied to Malabar. Larger investment decisions remain ahead, with the immediate focus on fully ramping the Maxwell Mine before committing to any significant new capital in these adjacent areas.

Supportive Thermal Coal Market Backdrop

Ongoing conflict in the Middle East is expected to sustain volatility in energy markets, supporting thermal coal as a reliable baseload power source. Management suggested that continued supply concerns underpin demand for coal generation, benefiting the pricing environment for New Hope’s products.

Strengthened Safety Controls and Engagement

In response to a rise in high‑potential and serious events across the industry, the group implemented safety pauses and increased frontline engagement. Targeted reviews and verification of critical controls were undertaken, with fatal and serious‑harm risk management reaffirmed as a top priority.

Organic Growth as Core Strategy

Management reiterated that strategic focus remains on organic growth across existing assets rather than major external deals. They said no external opportunity currently fits the portfolio, suggesting capital will stay directed toward internal projects with clearer risk‑return profiles.

Rising High-Potential Event Frequency

While the total recordable injury frequency rate fell to 3.89, down 12% from the prior quarter, high‑potential event frequency worsened from 1.21 to 4.65. Management referenced two recent fatalities in the broader east‑coast mining sector, underscoring the seriousness of the safety challenge.

New Acland Quarterly Sales Impacted by Rail

New Acland’s quarterly coal sales slipped to 0.9 million tonnes, down 7% from the prior period. The decline was mainly due to rail cancellations across the network caused by protected industrial action at Queensland Rail, highlighting exposure to external logistics constraints.

Rail Path Constraints Weigh on Performance

Fourth‑quarter rail performance was hampered by industrial action at Queensland Rail and outages linked to the Cross River Rail project. These issues reduced available rail paths, constraining coal movements and limiting the ability to fully realize production gains in sales.

Bengalla Quarterly Unit Cost Volatility

Bengalla’s unit costs shifted from $84 per tonne in the first half to $74 in the third quarter and $84.50 in the fourth. Management attributed the higher fourth‑quarter rate to lower‑than‑planned sales, heavy waste movement following FY2025 weather and broader inflationary pressures.

Inflationary Pressures and Cost Control

Management said the company has been working to stay ahead of cost inflation seen across the industry over the past six months. Efforts are focused on tightening full‑year costs, with an emphasis on productivity and disciplined procurement to protect margins.

Cash Holdings Above Long-Term Target

Current cash balances sit higher than the level management ultimately wants to hold, though they plan to retain more cash than historically. The stance reflects a desire to mitigate funding and site‑stoppage risks, while still allowing room for shareholder returns and project funding.

Worker Contract Negotiations Ahead
